differences.what: Actual master reviewed: the adjacent garden opening is now a broad barred light at the independently read section bounds; the former flat shelf beyond the traced coping turn is removed.

T-2759: the terminal post is built where HABS sheet 2 draws it (circle fit to the plan's ring: centre W33.81/S46.20, radius 0.93 ft at the line's centre; built 0.9 ft) instead of T-2218's section-fitted S46.05 / 0.75 ft, which put the whole post inside the wall's end-on silhouette. It now stands about 0.6 ft proud of the wall's outer face, so in this view its shaft shows from grade to crown and the coping dies into its north side at about 4.45 ft, just above the crown's springing, as the section draws it. The three reconstructed lower tread ends are re-seated on the new surface. Evidence: docs/RESEARCH/glessner-terrace-terminal-T-2759/.

T-2879 ruled the plan against the section along S. Sheet 2's printed court chain (12'-6" + 12'-0" + 10'-0" + 12'-8" = 47'-2") governs, and the plan scan reproduces it: court face S26.99 for the printed 26.83, the bow's tangent on the east wing 39.42 for 39.33, the tower's south junction 61.27 for 61.33. Sheet 4 draws the same court shifted north, not rescaled: face 26.21, bow flank 38.66, so its bow is 12.45 ft across against the printed 12.5. Re-zeroed on the printed court face (+0.65 ft), its terminal post reads S46.0-47.3. The plan-built post, seen past the wall's end, shows S46.2-47.1, so the post agrees within 0.2 ft and stays where the plan puts it. The bow and the stair tower stay on the plan too (docs/RESEARCH/glessner-court-ruling-T-2879/). What this view still shows is the frame mix. The coping's traced profile and the two grilles were read at sheet 4's un-re-zeroed S, and the camera reads in that frame too. So the coping reaches the post 0.65 ft early, over a reconstructed shoulder, and in this view the brick wall end covers the post's north half (render S46.3) where the drawing shows the stone shaft from S45.4. T-2880 carries those readings and this camera onto the plan's frame. T-2880 did: the coping's traced knots, both grilles' clears and the garden light's north jamb are built 0.65 ft south, and this camera's eye moved 0.198 m south with them (principal column 800 is plan S39.96). Read on this render against the drawing's ink: the two grilles and their stone heads and sills sit on the drawn ones, the coping's descent follows the drawn curve to the post, and the post's shaft shows at x 1175-1222 against the drawn 1160-1238, 15 and 16 px, inside the ±20 px the solve gives its picks. The coping now meets the post where the drawing has it meet (about x 1165-1185, y 295-312), its reconstructed shoulder running inside the post rather than over the court.

Beyond the post, against the stair tower: the garden light's clear opening shows at x 1222-1432 against the drawn 1228-1495, and the tower drum's north edge about 60 px (1.0 ft) north of the drawn one at x 1506. Sheet 4 draws the drum wide (T-2879: re-zeroed it overruns the printed 10'-0" mass by 0.5 ft at the north), and the re-zeroed light would end inside the plan's drum, so its south jamb is held 0.23 ft short of the drum; which drawn end is right is not settled. Below the light, the court's two stone steps are shorter than drawn (upper tread to x 1360 against 1535, lower to 1502 against 1580) and the upper tread's top is about 20 px low; the grille's outer stone surround is narrower than the drawn frame. No camera translation or source-pick revision has concealed these residuals. T-2906 built and ruled them. Read on this render against the drawing's ink: the court's two stone steps are built to the drawing's length and height. The upper tread's top now stands at sheet 4's 1.57 ft (y 427.5 against the drawn 430) and runs to x 1532 against the drawn 1535 (plan S52.30, where it meets the drum). The lower tread's top is at 0.88 ft (y 470 against 471), ending at x 1570 against 1577. The light is set in the drawing's broad dressed-stone panel, from the post to the drum and from the upper step (y 427.5) to its top at y 152.5 against the drawn 151.5; its left edge, behind the post, is at x 1144 against 1147. RULED, the light's south end against the drum: the panel and the light end at the built drum, x 1441, where the drawing ends them on its own drum line at x 1510. That 1.1 ft is the drum, not the light. Sheet 4 draws the drum 11.09 ft across against sheet 2's printed 10'-0" mass. T-2879 kept the plan's drum, and this view still shows that disagreement. The light keeps the drawing's own 0.23 ft stone margin to the drum, so its clear opening is 3.55 ft against the drawn 4.51. To show the drawn width, the light would have to end inside the drum.

T-2906: the lowest two treads' tops are the drawing's (1.57 and 0.88 ft), and the seven treads above them share the rest of the rise to the deck evenly (0.56 ft risers, against 0.61 before). The cheek wall hides those treads in this view. Their wall ends follow the drum, so the upper tread meets the wall under the light, with no pocket left between the stair and the wall.
Iron/frame stock and masonry color/weathering remain bounded reconstructions.

T-2928: the barred basement light beside the stair tower takes sheet 4's bar pitch (twelve bars drawn at 0.345 ft across the full drawn width; nine at 0.355 ft on the built light, which T-2880 holds short of the plan's drum), where it had six. Its rails and opening are unchanged.

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153).
